author: Today I Found Out
description:
On May 12, 2002, the roof of Building 112, a large hangar at the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan, suddenly collapsed, killing seven construction workers. It also destroyed several satellite preparation clean rooms, an Energia heavy-lift booster, and a Space Shuttle. 

No, not the iconic American Space Shuttle - more properly known as the Space Transport System or STS - but rather its Soviet and quite superior counterpart, Buran. 

Developed in direct response to the American Shuttle program, Buran flew only a single, unmanned mission in 1988 before the entire programme was cancelled following the collapse of the Soviet Union. Despite this, however, in many ways Buran was actually a superior design to its American counterpart, and had it entered regular service might have better have accomplished the Shuttle’s original goal of making manned spaceflight cheaper, safer, and more routine. title: Was the Soviet Space Shuttle Better Than NASA's?
